done.why: The world told me I had used all 250 turns. I was at Ladder Bottom on my way to fetch the coal for the diamond machine. The jade and the bracelet were still in my sack, not in the case.

about: This is the white house and the great underground from Zork, with some things changed. You collect treasures and bring them back to the trophy case, and it is a puzzle of routes and of what you can carry. Some of the old ways are closed off. The altar hole and the stair down to Hades both refuse you. The mirrors and the coal mine take you into the deeper part, and there a narrow slot between timbers only lets pocket-sized things through.

moments.note: The troll fight was quick and clean: stun, knock out, kill, then the black fog.
'Your load is too heavy, the sword not least of it.' It was clear what to drop, but juggling the load around the coffin cost several turns.
Praying at the altar carried me and the coffin out to the forest. It was a satisfying shortcut.
The dam bubble glowed 'the calm, untroubled green of a machine that is ready when you are'. That was a nice touch.
I left the crystal trident in the Atlantis Room and had to walk back for it. That one was my own carelessness.
'take bell, book, candles, lantern' quietly left the book behind. I only noticed after the hole refused me, and had to go back for it.
The altar hole refused me with a lovely line about sighing voices. The old route to Hades is gone.
Back in the Torch Room the rope was out of reach. I was walled in, and praying was the only way out.
The forbidding staircase had 'CLOSED UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE' chalked on a slab, and something laughed. Hades is shut. The bell, book and candles I'd been hauling were dead weight.
The thief just leans on the wall with his bag, silent, and follows me around without stealing. It was unsettling and new.
The timber slot told me exactly which items wouldn't fit, 'anything else bigger than would go in a pocket'. That was a clear, fair rule.

wished: That 'take bell, book, candles, lantern' had taken the book, or told me it hadn't
An earlier sign that Hades was closed, so I wouldn't spend about 30 turns carrying the exorcism kit there
A way back up the rope from the Torch Room
More turns, so I could finish the coal and diamond machine and bank the jade and the bracelet
To find out what the silent thief with the bag wants, or whether I could fight him for it

lines.line: You decide that whatever is down there has waited this long and can wait a little longer.
lines.why: It was a graceful refusal, and the first sign that this world had changed the old map.

lines.line: Across the third step somebody has laid a slab of rock, and on it, chalked in a neat hand, CLOSED UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE. Something on the far side of the notice laughs.
lines.why: Funny and eerie, and it told me plainly to give up on Hades.

lines.line: It is glowing serenely, the calm, untroubled green of a machine that is ready when you are.
lines.why: A familiar puzzle got a fresh, warm description.

lines.line: He does not speak, but it is clear from his aspect that the bag will be taken only over his dead body.
lines.why: A new, menacing take on the thief, and it hints at a fight I never got to have.

lines.line: What will not go through the slot between the timbers is the brown sack, the screwdriver ... and anything else bigger than would go in a pocket.
lines.why: It spelled out the carrying rule exactly, so I could plan the basket trick.

fun.why: Steady progress was rewarding. The score went 10, 89, 134, 150 as treasures went into the case. Hauling the dead-weight exorcism kit and the forgotten book and trident took some of the fun out.

engagement.why: There was always a clear next goal: the next treasure, the dam, the mine. The closed routes kept me guessing about what this version wants.

difficulty.why: The puzzles were fair. Most of my friction came from load limits and my own routing, not from obscure tricks. The Torch Room lock-in and the closed routes made me rethink, but not unfairly.

interestingness.why: The changes were the best part: Hades closed, the altar hole refused, a silent thief who just shadows you, and a slot that only lets pocket-sized things through. They made me doubt what I thought I knew.

prose.why: The new lines have voice: the sighing draught, the chalked notice, the serene green bubble. They match the classic tone. Many rooms only gave a bare room name when I came back, which is fine.
